rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Structural isomerism** rewires the same atoms five ways. **Chain isomerism** changes the skeleton (butane/2-methylpropane; the three C₅H₁₂ isomers). **Position isomerism** slides one group along an unchanged skeleton (propan-1-ol/propan-2-ol). **Functional isomerism** swaps the group itself, jumping homologous series (ethanol/dimethyl ether; propanal/propanone).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Chain: C₄H₁₀ → butane / 2-methylpropane; C₅H₁₂ → 3 isomers - Position: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH / CH₃CHOHCH₃ - Functional: C₂H₆O → CH₃CH₂OH / CH₃OCH₃ - Metamerism: C₂H₅–O–C₂H₅ / CH₃–O–C₃H₇ - Tautomerism: CH₃CHO ⇌ CH₂=CH–OH

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Covers only: structural isomerism, its types: chain isomerism, position isomerism, functional isomerism (within Fundamental Principles of Organic Chemistry).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Structural isomerism is the existence of compounds with the same molecular formula but different connectivity, classified as chain, position, functional isomerism, metamerism and tautomerism."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***C5H12's three skeletons*** — n-pentane, isopentane and neopentane share one formula but differ only in branching: chain isomerism at its cleanest, with boiling points falling 36 -> 28 -> 9.5 C as branching increases.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Five Ways to Rewire the Same Atoms Structural isomerism is connectivity chemistry: the same atoms, joined differently, give different compounds. Five sub-types cover it — **chain, position, functional, metamerism and tautomerism** — and each has a signature pair that examiners love. Learn the diagnostic question each type answers and you can classify any pair on sight.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Chain (skeletal) isomerism - Same formula, **different carbon skeletons** — straight vs branched. - C₄H₁₀: **butane** (straight) / **2-methylpropane** (branched). C₅H₁₂: n-pentane, isopentane (2-methylbutane), neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane) — three chain isomers. ### 2.2 Position isomerism - Same skeleton **and** same functional group; the group sits on **different carbons**.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Chain = skeleton; position = moved group; functional = new group; metamerism = changed alkyl flanks (O/N/C=O between them); tautomerism = keto <=> enol with alpha-H. Signature pairs: C4H10, propanols, C2H6O, C4H10O ethers, CH3CHO.

Explain chain, position and functional isomerism with one example each.** — **Structural isomerism** is the phenomenon in which compounds have the **same molecular formula but different connectivity** — their atoms are joined in different arrangements.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): What is metamerism? Give an example.** — **Metamerism** is a form of structural isomerism in which compounds share the **same functional group** but differ in the **alkyl groups attached on either side of the polyvalent atom or group** (oxygen in ethers, nitrogen in amines, the carbonyl carbon in ketones).…

rows.text: When asked to "explain with example", write both structures of the pair and name the differing feature explicitly — the named feature is the mark.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Five diagnostic questions sort any pair: different skeleton? moved group? different group? different alkyl flanks? dynamic H-shift? — structural isomerism is a decision tree, not a memory list.

Common Confusions **Metamerism is not position isomerism:** in metamerism the *groups attached to the polyvalent atom* change (ethyl/ethyl → methyl/propyl); position isomerism slides one group along an unchanged skeleton.  ·  **Enols are not isolable curiosities:** the keto form usually dominates (>99%), but the tiny enol fraction drives reactions like halogenation of ketones.

rows.label: More ideas
